glance_notes.text: Same-Day Voter Registration: Vermont has no advance voter registration deadline. Eligible residents may register before an election or at their polling place on Election Day. An eligible applicant whose registration is approved at the polling place is added to the checklist and may vote.

General Election Ballots Mailed Automatically: For every Vermont General Election, the Secretary of State mails a ballot to every active voter on the statewide voter checklist. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, voters should make sure their registration and mailing address are current before the statewide mailing list is prepared.

Polls Close at 7:00 p.m.: All Vermont polling places close at 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. Opening times are set locally and may vary, but polls must open no later than 10:00 a.m. and may open as early as 5:00 a.m.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Vermont residents may register to vote online through the state's My Voter Page system, through a voter registration agency, by submitting an application to their town or city clerk, or at their polling place on Election Day. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, be a resident of Vermont and the town where the person seeks to vote, take the Voter's Oath and meet Vermont's age requirements. A person who will be 18 years old on or before the date of a General Election may register before turning 18 under Vermont law.
register.glance_value: Online, clerk's office or Election Day registration
register.source_name: Vermont Secretary of State — Voter Registration
register.internal_note: Vermont has Election Day registration and should not be given a conventional pre-election registration cutoff. Vermont law expressly permits an application to be delivered to the presiding officer before polls close. The Secretary of State's My Voter Page at [https://vote.vermont.gov/](https://vote.vermont.gov/) provides online registration. Vermont also requires the Voter's Oath for first-time Vermont registrants.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Vermont's My Voter Page to check voter registration, update voter information, request an early or absentee ballot when necessary, track a ballot, find polling-place information and view voter-specific election information. Voters should make sure their mailing address is current before General Election ballots are prepared for statewide mailing.
check_registration.source_name: Vermont Secretary of State — My Voter Page
check_registration.internal_note: My Voter Page is Vermont's official voter-facing portal. Address accuracy is particularly important because Vermont automatically mails General Election ballots to active voters using the statewide voter checklist.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: Vermont does not have a traditional advance voter registration deadline. Eligible residents may register before Election Day or at their polling place on Election Day. An Election Day registration application must be submitted before the polls close, and election officials must determine that the applicant meets Vermont's voter qualifications before adding the voter to the checklist and allowing the voter to vote.
deadlines.glance_value: Election Day registration available until polls close
deadlines.internal_note: 17 V.S.A. § 2144 expressly permits Election Day registration during voting hours. Section 2144a also permits a registration application to be delivered to the presiding officer before the close of polls. Do not invent a conventional October registration deadline for Vermont.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use Vermont's My Voter Page or contact your town or city clerk to find your Election Day polling place. Vermont towns establish their polling locations locally, and towns with multiple polling places assign voters according to their residence. Polling locations can change, so voters should confirm their location before Election Day.
polling_place.glance_value: Find your polling place through My Voter Page
polling_place.source_name: Vermont Secretary of State — My Voter Page
polling_place.internal_note: Vermont's local election administration makes town-specific verification important. Under 17 V.S.A. § 2521, town clerks must post an election warning at least 30 days before an election that includes the polling-place location and election hours.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Vermont's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. All polling places close at 7:00 p.m. Opening times are established locally and may range from 5:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. A qualified voter who is present at the polling place at 7:00 p.m. and has not yet been able to vote must be given a reasonable opportunity to cast a ballot. Eligible residents may also register at the polling place on Election Day.
election_day.glance_value: Polls close at 7:00 p.m.; opening time varies by town
election_day.internal_note: Vermont does not have a uniform statewide opening time. Under 17 V.S.A. § 2561, Australian-ballot polls may open no earlier than 5:00 a.m. and must open no later than 10:00 a.m., as set by each town's board of civil authority. All close at 7:00 p.m. Voters present at closing who have been unable to vote must be allowed a reasonable opportunity to do so.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Vermont polling-place opening times vary by municipality. Under state law, polls may open as early as 5:00 a.m. and must open no later than 10:00 a.m. All polling places close at 7:00 p.m. Voters should check My Voter Page or their town or city clerk for their specific polling-place opening time.
polling_hours.glance_value: Open 5:00–10:00 a.m. depending on town; close 7:00 p.m.
polling_hours.internal_note: Do not state a single statewide opening time. Vermont statute gives municipalities discretion within the 5:00 a.m.-10:00 a.m. window. The statewide closing time is 7:00 p.m.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Vermont allows no-excuse early or absentee voting. Once ballots are available, a registered voter may obtain a ballot from the town or city clerk and vote it in the clerk's office. The voter may mark and return the ballot immediately or take the ballot and return it under Vermont's early-ballot procedures. Availability and clerk-office hours vary by municipality, so voters should contact their clerk or use official local election information for exact dates and hours.
early_voting.glance_value: No excuse; vote at your town or city clerk once ballots are available
early_voting.internal_note: Vermont's early voting is legally part of its early or absentee voting system rather than a separately standardized statewide early-voting period with uniform locations and hours. Section 2537 permits in-person voting at the town clerk's office once ballots are available. Ballots must be furnished to town clerks no later than 45 days before an election under 17 V.S.A. § 2479.

absentee_mail.label: Early / Absentee Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Vermont allows any voter to vote early or absentee without providing an excuse. For every General Election, the Secretary of State automatically mails a ballot and postage-paid return envelope to every active voter on the statewide voter checklist. State law requires the mailing to begin no later than 43 days before the election and be completed no later than October 1. Voters who need a ballot sent to a different address should update their information or request the appropriate delivery through their town or city clerk or My Voter Page. A voter may separately request an early or absentee ballot until 5:00 p.m. or the closing of the town clerk's office on the day before the election, subject to the clerk's office schedule. Mailed voted ballots must reach the town clerk before polls close on Election Day.
absentee_mail.glance_value: General Election ballots automatically mailed to all active voters
absentee_mail.internal_note: This is a major Vermont distinction. Since Act 60 of 2021, the Secretary of State must mail a General Election ballot to every active voter. The mailing must commence no later than 43 days before Election Day and finish by October 1. Under 17 V.S.A. § 2531, separately requested absentee ballots can generally be requested through 5:00 p.m. or clerk-office closing on the day preceding the election. Under § 2543, mailed ballots must reach the town clerk before polls close Election Day. Do not describe Election Day postmarking as sufficient.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Vermont generally does not require already-registered voters to present photo identification simply to vote at the polls. Federal law does require certain first-time voters who registered by mail or online and whose identifying information was not previously verified to provide qualifying identification or documentation. Those voters may satisfy the requirement before Election Day or at the polls. A voter subject to this first-time-voter requirement who does not provide the required identification may have the ballot handled under Vermont's provisional-voting procedures.
voter_id.glance_value: No general photo-ID requirement for established registered voters
voter_id.source_name: Vermont Secretary of State — Voter Registration
voter_id.internal_note: Do not label Vermont a photo-ID state. The important exception derives from HAVA and applies to certain first-time voters who registered by mail or online and have not satisfied identity-verification requirements. 17 V.S.A. § 2546 also specifically provides that an early ballot from such a first-time voter is treated as provisional if required identification has not been submitted before polls close.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Vermont provides accessible voting systems and voter assistance for voters with disabilities. Federal elections require an accessible voting method that allows voters with disabilities, including voters who are blind or visually impaired, to vote privately and independently. A voter who needs assistance marking a ballot may receive assistance under Vermont law. Voters who cannot conveniently vote at a polling place may also use Vermont's no-excuse early or absentee voting options. Voters needing a specific accommodation should contact their town or city clerk before voting.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible voting system, assistance and absentee options
accessible_voting.source_name: Vermont Secretary of State — Voting Accessibility
accessible_voting.internal_note: 17 V.S.A. §§ 2567 and 2569 govern accessible voting systems and voter assistance. Vermont's local administration means voters needing a specific physical accommodation should confirm arrangements with the municipal clerk. Vermont also authorizes mobile polling stations under § 2532a when approved by the Secretary of State.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Vermont provides special registration and absentee-voting procedures for eligible members of the uniformed services, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living outside the United States under federal UOCAVA requirements. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request an absentee ballot and may use the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot when eligible. Vermont permits electronic transmission of voting materials to qualifying military and overseas voters. Because deadlines and electronic-return procedures can differ from ordinary absentee voting, covered voters should use the current Vermont Secretary of State military and overseas instructions for the 2026 General Election.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA and FWAB available; special UOCAVA procedures apply
military_overseas.source_name: Vermont Secretary of State — Military and Overseas Voters
military_overseas.flagged_reason: Vermont's general UOCAVA procedures are established, but the exact 2026 voter-facing transmission and return deadlines should be rechecked against the Secretary of State's final November 2026 military and overseas instructions before publication.
military_overseas.internal_note: Avoid importing ordinary domestic absentee deadlines into UOCAVA guidance. Federal law requires timely transmission of requested ballots to covered voters, and Vermont provides military/overseas-specific procedures. Reverify exact November 2026 deadlines and permitted electronic return methods from the Secretary of State's current UOCAVA instructions close to the election.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Vermont if they meet Vermont's voter eligibility and residency requirements and consider the Vermont address their voting residence. A student may vote in only one jurisdiction for an election. Students who establish Vermont voting residency may register online, through their town clerk or on Election Day. Students who remain registered elsewhere should follow the voting and absentee rules of that jurisdiction instead. Vermont does not generally require an already-registered voter to present a student ID or other photo ID simply to vote, although certain first-time voters may be subject to federal identification requirements.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may register at a qualifying Vermont voting residence
student_voting.source_name: Vermont Secretary of State — Voter Registration
student_voting.internal_note: Do not imply that attending a Vermont college automatically creates voting residency. Vermont registration depends on residency under state law. Also do not describe a college ID as generally required for voting because Vermont has no general photo-ID-at-the-polls requirement.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Vermont voters can use My Voter Page and their town or city clerk's election information to review voter-specific ballot information when available. Ballots vary according to the voter's municipality and legislative districts. State law also requires towns to post an election warning at least 30 days before the election describing the offices and questions to be voted upon.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Check My Voter Page and your municipal clerk
sample_ballot.source_name: Vermont Secretary of State — My Voter Page
sample_ballot.internal_note: 17 V.S.A. § 2521 requires municipal election warnings at least 30 days before the election and requires the warning to identify offices and questions being voted upon. My Voter Page is the appropriate voter-specific state portal. Reverify once final November 2026 ballot information is populated.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 128 State Street, Montpelier, VT 05633. Phone: 802-828-2363. Office hours are generally 7:45 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday, except state holidays. For voter-specific registration, ballot, polling-place or local election questions, voters should also contact their town or city clerk.
contact.source_name: Vermont Secretary of State — Elections Division
contact.internal_note: The State of Vermont's current official directory verifies the Secretary of State at 128 State Street, Montpelier, VT 05633-1101 and 802-828-2363. The Elections Division's current state pages list office hours of 7:45 a.m.-4:30 p.m. Monday-Friday except holidays. No uncertain general elections email was inserted into reader-facing content.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Vermont Secretary of State Elections Division, My Voter Page and your town or city clerk for official election information. These resources provide voter registration, voter-record updates, polling-place information, early and absentee voting information, ballot tracking, accessibility information, military and overseas voting guidance and voter-specific election information. Vermont's municipal clerks administer voter checklists, local polling places, early voting and the receipt of absentee ballots.
official_resources.glance_value: Secretary of State, My Voter Page & municipal clerks
official_resources.source_name: Vermont Secretary of State — Elections Division
official_resources.internal_note: Official Vermont Elections Division: [https://sos.vermont.gov/elections/](https://sos.vermont.gov/elections/). Official My Voter Page: [https://vote.vermont.gov/](https://vote.vermont.gov/). Official voter registration information: [https://sos.vermont.gov/elections/voters/registration/](https://sos.vermont.gov/elections/voters/registration/). Official early and absentee voting information: [https://sos.vermont.gov/elections/voters/early-absentee-voting/](https://sos.vermont.gov/elections/voters/early-absentee-voting/). Vermont General Election automatic-mail-ballot law: [https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/17/051/02537a](https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/17/051/02537a). Vermont Election Day registration law: [https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/17/043/02144](https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/17/043/02144). Vermont polling-hours law: [https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/17/051/02561](https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/17/051/02561). Vermont absentee-ballot return law: [https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/17/051/02543](https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/17/051/02543).
